note: Professionally he reads as ICP — an engineer with a settled career, a family and enough autonomy to train seven times a week — and he is the clearest good-to-great case in the batch after Roy Norman, rating himself a seven out of ten and articulating exactly what the missing three points look like. Not deconditioned is beyond argument: 145 lb at 5'4", visible abs emerging, a former state-level wrestler who competes in Masters division boxing. The two misses repeat a pattern now visible across this whole batch. Income fails outright — his stated ceiling is $100-150 per month against a $4,000 minimum, and he corrected the rep to make clear it was a budget constraint and not a value judgement. And health is not his neglected domain; it is the domain he has already optimised, so the offer arrives as a marginal upgrade to a functioning system rather than as the fix for a gap. That is now the third prospect in two days — with Roy Norman and Soneel Raj — where health is the strongest rather than the weakest area, and the two calls where income also failed both ended without a sale. The stated ICP is describing a profile that keeps arriving on calls while failing the one criterion that determines whether anyone buys.
